messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PDR-84712 -> PG primary connection queueing spike detected. CPU 94%, active connections 5.2k (limit 5k), replication lag rising. Auto-page to oncall.

pagerduty: Paging Samir (oncall) for PDR-84712 (pg-primary-conn-queue). Severity: high. <https://pagerduty.example/incident/PDR-84712>

Samir (oncall): acked. I'll triage, tagging db lead. @Jin can you jump in? I'll start mitigation checklist.

Maya: seeing 502s from /v1/generate and client timeouts. Traffic spike started ~00:12 UTC, correlates with a batch job retry loop from a partner. Can we put a short app-layer throttle while we stabilize the DB?

Samir (oncall): good idea. Lia, can you flip the rate limit rule for /v1/generate to 20r/s per IP in the WAF? That should cut load by ~60%.

Lia: on it. Pushing rule now — will take ~30s to propagate.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: "Postgres connection storm" recommended actions: 1) check pg_stat_activity, 2) identify long-running queries, 3) apply pgbouncer emergency settings, 4) consider selective read routing. Link: https://runbooks.redwood/pg-conn-storm

Samir (oncall): running quick checks:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='active';
SELECT datname, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY datname ORDER BY 2 DESC;
SELECT pid, now()-query_start AS duration, state, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='active' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 10;
```

Samir (oncall): pg_stat_activity shows ~4200 active on inference-db, top offenders are a repeated INSERT INTO usage_events and several idle-in-transaction sessions from a background worker. pgbouncer shows bridge queueing. I can increment pgbouncer pool size temporarily and enable transaction pooling for the bursty clients.

Jin (db): I see the same. Before we change pooling, cancel the longest-running abusive queries and pause the partner consumer if possible. Also we should not failover immediately — replication lag is rising and a forced failover will make things worse.

Maya: partner confirmed they have a retry bug and paused their job. We've seen 12 customers with high error rates and a few internal jobs failing. Impact: degraded latency and 5xxs on inference-hosted endpoints; non-urgent background indexing is affected too.

Samir (oncall): Lia — any update on WAF throttle? If that removes most traffic we can do less invasive DB work.

Lia: WAF rule live. Traffic to /v1/generate down ~62% from peak, 5xx rate dropping. Visual confirms queue depth decreasing.

Samir (oncall): Lia nice. I'm going to apply emergency pgbouncer bump on the primary pool, adjust pool_size and reserve_pool_count. Commands in config push:
```
# /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini (apply via config push)
pool_size = 200
reserve_pool = 50
reserve_pool_timeout = 10
transaction_mode = 1
```

Samir (oncall): applied via orchestration. Restarting pgbouncer gracefully.

ops-runbook-bot: Action note logged: pgbouncer config bump + WAF throttle. Ticket created: ICS-532.

Jin (db): I'm canceling the runaway INSERTs and killing lingering idle-in-transaction sessions after a short warning. Also adding a temporary statement_timeout of 30s for the offending DB user to prevent long locks.

Samir (oncall): executing cancel for pid 34211, 34209. Setting statement_timeout for user "worker_user":
```
ALTER ROLE worker_user SET statement_timeout = '30s';
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(34211);
```

Maya: metrics: error rate back to 1.8% (was 13%), response times halved. Customer impact still present for those 12 customers but mostly degraded not fully down.

Jin (db): replication lag peaked at 18s, now down to 4s. The pgbouncer bump bought us headroom; connection queueing resolved. I recommend we keep throttles and timeouts for 30m and then re-evaluate.

Samir (oncall): Agreed. I'll document mitigations and handoff to Lia for the night shift. Lia, please keep the throttles and watch 1) active connections, 2) replication lag, 3) 5xx rate for /v1/generate.

Lia: taking handoff. I'll escalate back to Samir if connections > 4500 or 5xx > 5% sustained for 5m. Also will check scheduled jobs to avoid recurrence. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident PDR-84712 acknowledged by Samir. Assigned to team: infra-db.

Samir (oncall): Creating incident summary for postmortem and notifying CS for customer outreach. Draft notes:
- Root cause: partner retry loop created connection surge overwhelming pgbouncer; background workers held idle-in-transaction.
- Mitigations: WAF throttle, pgbouncer emergency pool increase, cancel long queries, set statement_timeout, partner paused job.
- Impact: ~12 customers experienced elevated errors and latency for ~22 minutes; no data corruption.

Maya: I'll coordinate customer comms with CS. Sending tentative message: we mitigated the issue, continuing to monitor, will follow up with RCA.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident resolved by runbook steps? Mark 'in-progress' until PD closes.

Samir (oncall): Closing notes: will open a follow-up engineering task to implement automated backpressure detection + graceful circuit-breaker at service edge to avoid DB flooding. Also propose adding a pgbouncer autoscale slider for bursts.

pagerduty: Incident PDR-84712 status: RESOLVED by Samir at 1769990321. Resolution summary: aggressive client retries were throttled; pgbouncer tuned; DB long-running sessions terminated. Postmortem ticket: PMT-289.

incident-bot: Thread closed. Please file postmortem in incidents/ and tag postmortem-required.
